question_text: The refractive index of material of prism is $\sqrt{2}$. Angle of prism $A$ is equal to
solution: For a prism in the minimum deviation position, the refracted ray is parallel to the base so $r = A/2$. With symmetric incidence at $i = 45^\circ$, $\sin r = \frac{\sin 45^\circ}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{2} \implies r = 30^\circ$, giving $A = 2r = 60^\circ$.

question_text: A convex lens forms the image of an object of same magnification when the object is placed at $10\text{ cm}$ and $20\text{ cm}$ from the lens. The focal length of the lens is
solution: Since the magnifications are equal in magnitude but opposite in sign (one real, one virtual), $\frac{f}{f - u_1} = -\frac{f}{f - u_2}$, which gives $f = \frac{u_1 + u_2}{2} = \frac{10 + 20}{2} = 15\text{ cm}$.

question_text: A small source of light is $2\text{ m}$ below the surface of a liquid of refractive index $\frac{5}{3}$. In order to block all the light coming out of the liquid surface, the minimum diameter of the disc placed on the surface of the liquid is
solution: Critical angle satisfies $\sin C = \frac{1}{\mu} = \frac{3}{5}$, so $\tan C = \frac{3}{4}$. The radius is $r = h\tan C = 2 \times \frac{3}{4} = 1.5\text{ m}$, giving a minimum diameter of $d = 2r = 3\text{ m}$.

question_text: A glass slab is placed with the right angle prism as shown in the figure. The possible value of $\theta$ such that light incident normally on the prism does not pass through the glass slab is
solution: For total internal reflection at the prism-slab interface, $i = 90^\circ - \theta \ge C$. Here, $\sin C = \frac{1.2}{1.5} = \frac{4}{5} \implies C = 53^\circ$. Thus, $90^\circ - \theta \ge 53^\circ \implies \theta \le 37^\circ$, which is satisfied by both $30^\circ$ and $37^\circ$.
